sections.title: Unit Overview

blocks.text: The Akron General Neuroscience ICU is a fully operational 10-bed Neuro ICU within a Comprehensive Stroke Center and a Level I Trauma Center. The unit provides multidisciplinary, evidence-based care for patients with complex neurological and neurosurgical conditions, including acute stroke, traumatic brain injury, intracranial hemorrhage, status epilepticus, spinal cord injury, and other critical neurologic illnesses.

blocks.text: The NSICU team serves as the primary admitting service for patients with:

Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH)

sections.title: Isolated Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI)

blocks.text: Patients with isolated moderate-to-severe TBI are admitted under the Trauma Surgery service.
The NSICU team provides all neurocritical care management in collaboration with the Trauma Surgery and Neurosurgery teams.
Following completion of the tertiary trauma survey and clearance by the Trauma service, primary responsibility for patient management is transferred to the NSICU team.

sections.title: Airway & Emergency Response

blocks.text: The NSICU attending is responsible for airway management for patients admitted under the NSICU service between 7:00 AM and 5:00 PM.
The NSICU team responds to medical emergencies and Code Blue events involving NSICU patients.
NSICU Advanced Practice Providers (APPs) do not perform endotracheal intubation; airway management is the responsibility of the attending physician.
After 5:00 PM, the MICU team provides airway management and emergency response support for NSICU patients.

sections.title: 8:45 AM - Multidisciplinary Discharge Planning Rounds

blocks.text: Primary objectives:
Review each patient's overall clinical status and anticipated discharge needs.
Discuss barriers to discharge and care transitions.
Review the ongoing need for invasive lines and devices (e.g., central venous catheters, arterial lines, Foley catheters) and place removal orders when appropriate.
Coordinate rehabilitation and post-acute care planning.

The multidisciplinary team includes Care Management, Bedside Nursing, Physical Therapy (PT), Occupational Therapy (OT), Speech-Language Pathology (SLP), and additional disciplines as needed. These collaborative rounds facilitate early discharge planning and ensure coordinated, patient-centered stroke and neurocritical care.

sections.title: Inpatient Neurology Support

blocks.text: All patients admitted to the NSICU with acute ischemic stroke, intracerebral hemorrhage, or other complex neurological disorders should receive a Neurology consultation.

sections.title: Auto Launch & the CCT Process

blocks.text: Transfer line: 216-448-7000 (Cleveland Clinic Critical Care Transport dispatch)

At Cleveland Clinic, the auto launch process is an expedited emergency transfer protocol. It quickly transports patients with life-threatening conditions (such as heart attacks or strokes) from regional hospitals to definitive care.

sections.title: Acute Stroke / ICH Transfer Workflow

rows: A referring hospital identifies a patient with acute ischemic stroke, ICH, SAH, large vessel occlusion (LVO), or another time-sensitive neurological emergency requiring a higher level of care.
The referring physician contacts the Cleveland Clinic Critical Care Transport (CCT) dispatch center through the dedicated transfer line to initiate an emergency transfer.

Following acceptance by the receiving physician, CCT immediately dispatches the most appropriate resource (helicopter, fixed-wing, or mobile ICU ambulance). Transport begins while the receiving team coordinates bed placement.

Neurocritical Care, Stroke Neurology, Neurosurgery, and/or Neuroendovascular teams are notified per diagnosis. Brain imaging is electronically transferred and reviewed when available. Treatment plans (thrombolysis, thrombectomy, neurosurgical intervention, neurocritical care) are developed before arrival. The receiving ICU, angio suite, OR, or ED is prepared. Communication is facilitated by Epic Secure Chat, CCF iPhone messaging, and direct phone calls.

On arrival the patient goes directly to the appropriate destination: Neuro ICU, microangiography suite (mechanical thrombectomy), OR, or ED (if additional stabilization is needed). A structured physician-to-physician and nurse-to-nurse handoff ensures continuity and timely definitive treatment.

GUIDING PRINCIPLE - TIME IS BRAIN · Early activation of transport, multidisciplinary communication, and parallel preparation of the receiving team are essential to minimize treatment delays and optimize neurological outcomes.

sections.title: Diagnoses Eligible for Emergency Transfer (Incl. Auto Launch)

blocks.text: Acute ischemic stroke within the treatment window for thrombolysis and/or mechanical thrombectomy
Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH)
Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH)
Cerebral edema with impending or established brain herniation
Status epilepticus or refractory seizures
Moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury (TBI)
Acute hydrocephalus

blocks.text: ICU Consent (SmartPhrase: .nicuconsent)

The APP is not credentialed for independent airway management; therefore, informed consent for ICU-level procedures should be obtained upon admission whenever feasible. ICU consent includes authorization for routine critical care interventions, including but not limited to:
Endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation
Central venous catheter placement
Arterial line placement
Blood product transfusion
Pulmonary artery catheter insertion
Bronchoscopy and related diagnostic/therapeutic procedures
Lumbar puncture (LP)
These procedures are considered part of standard ICU care and may be performed as clinically indicated.

Hospice services should be involved for all patients transitioning to comfort measures only (CMO) to ensure coordination of care, symptom control, and family support.
Palliative Care consultation services are typically led by Dr. Scanling and her team.
Use the Med Comfort Care order set in Epic to standardize symptom management and ensure consistency in end-of-life care delivery.

sections.title: Organ Donation - LifeBanc

blocks.text: LifeBanc is the designated Organ Procurement Organization (OPO) for Northeast Ohio and partners with Cleveland Clinic Health System.
Patients meeting established referral criteria are automatically referred to LifeBanc.
Before withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment or initiation of brain death evaluation, ensure LifeBanc has been notified. The bedside RN may contact the OPO if needed.

rows: CMS REQUIREMENT · Only LifeBanc/OPO personnel may discuss organ and tissue donation with the patient's family. The treating clinical team must not initiate donation discussions before OPO involvement.

sections.title: Death by Neurologic Criteria (DNC)

blocks.text: All intensivists performing DNC evaluations must follow the Cleveland Clinic Health System (CCHS) DNC Policy.
Providers must have approved DNC privileges before independently performing DNC evaluations.
The CCHS DNC Policy and Procedure (Determination of Death by Neurological Criteria in Adults, v.5) is available on the CCHS Intranet under Policies & Procedures.
MyLearning requirement: all intensivists must complete the DNC MyLearning module every 2 years. Completion is required to obtain and maintain DNC privileges.

sections.title: Neuromonitoring

blocks.text: Patients requiring invasive neuromonitoring should, whenever possible, be admitted to the NeuroICU (3200).

If no NeuroICU bed is available, or in selected high-injury-severity polytrauma cases, patients may be managed in one of the two neuromonitoring-capable beds on the 4th Floor ICU, at the discretion of the Trauma team.

sections.title: Acute Stroke / ICH Transfer Workflow

rows: A referring hospital identifies a patient with acute ischemic stroke, ICH, SAH, large vessel occlusion (LVO), or another time-sensitive neurological emergency requiring a higher level of care.
The referring physician contacts the Cleveland Clinic Critical Care Transport (CCT) dispatch center through the dedicated transfer line to initiate an emergency transfer.

Following acceptance by the receiving physician, CCT immediately dispatches the most appropriate resource (helicopter, fixed-wing, or mobile ICU ambulance). Transport begins while the receiving team coordinates bed placement.

Neurocritical Care, Stroke Neurology, Neurosurgery, and/or Neuroendovascular teams are notified per diagnosis. Brain imaging is electronically transferred and reviewed when available. Treatment plans (thrombolysis, thrombectomy, neurosurgical intervention, neurocritical care) are developed before arrival. The receiving ICU, angio suite, OR, or ED is prepared. Communication is facilitated by Epic Secure Chat, CCF iPhone messaging, and direct phone calls.

On arrival the patient goes directly to the appropriate destination: Neuro ICU, microangiography suite (mechanical thrombectomy), OR, or ED (if additional stabilization is needed). A structured physician-to-physician and nurse-to-nurse handoff ensures continuity and timely definitive treatment.

Guiding Principle — Time Is Brain · Early activation of transport, multidisciplinary communication, and parallel preparation of the receiving team are essential to minimize treatment delays and optimize neurological outcomes.

Lumbar puncture (LP)
